acceptance: pr-open and pr-arm succeed in a cloud session using only REST (gh api) or CCR routes, with no GraphQL calls; they keep working locally
pr-arm keeps all current refusals (hold label, draft, base, changes requested, unresolved threads, head mismatch) and handles the 422 clean-status case with a head-pinned squash merge
worktree-create (or a sibling target) can attach an existing session branch without weakening the main-clone write guard
Missing shared pre-commit hook is installed or reported before worktree creation, with one documented command
The pre-commit node hooks run on the cloud image's Node version, or the repo pins/provisions a compatible Node (e.g. through the session-start hook)
Tests cover the GraphQL-free code paths in scripts/pr_arm.py and the pr-open recipe
description:
In a Claude Code cloud session (PR #3090, 2026-10-17), the documented PR flow (agent-write-preflight -> commit -> pr-preflight -> pr-open -> pr-arm) needed manual workarounds at five steps. Make each step work as-is in cloud containers, without weakening any gate.

Observed failures:
1. pr-open and pr-arm fail: `gh pr list/create/merge` use GraphQL, which the cloud proxy blocks ("HTTP 403: GitHub GraphQL is not available from Claude Code sessions; use the REST API"). The push inside pr-open succeeded; the PR was opened with the GitHub MCP tool instead. pr-arm's hold check had to be redone by hand via `gh api` REST.
2. Auto-merge: the REST route is `PUT /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/ccr/auto_merge`. It returns 422 "Pull request is in clean status" when the PR can already merge, so pr-arm needs a fallback: a squash merge pinned to the head SHA (`--match-head-commit` equivalent) when the PR is clean.
3. scripts/worktree_lifecycle.sh `create` refuses an existing local or remote branch. Cloud sessions are handed a fixed, pre-created branch, so `make worktree-create` cannot be used; the worktree was attached with a plain `git worktree add`.
4. agent-write-preflight requires the shared pre-commit hook in the primary clone. Fresh cloud clones don't have it, and the refusal only appears after the worktree exists.
5. markdownlint-cli pre-commit hook: npm fails with EBADENGINE (ini@7 needs node ^22.22.2; the container has 22.22.0 at /opt/node22). Worked around by putting Node 24 on PATH.

Also seen, out of scope unless cheap: the global git identity is Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>, which agent-write-preflight correctly refuses. The session needs a documented way to set the human author.
